tool_input.command:
git -C <repo> commit -am "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): exec-bit check no longer FAILs every Windows install

Moving the executable-bit check ahead of the sandbox call (qodo #3) was
correct on Unix but made the check run on Windows, where Go's os.Stat
derives a regular file's permission bits from the read-only attribute
alone (go1.26 os/types_windows.go, fileStat.mode: 0o444 or 0o666, with
0o111 added only for a directory). Perm()&0o111 == 0 therefore held for
every hook there: every enabled Windows install FAILed with an
unactionable `chmod +x`, and the qodo #12 unsupported-platform FAIL/WARN
split below it became unreachable. Regression introduced by this branch;
CI missed it because the doctor tests run on Linux.

Gate the check on sandboxGOOS != "windows" — the seam the package already
uses for its other Windows guard, and what makes both arms testable from
any host. The qodo #3 property is preserved exactly: on platforms where
the bit is meaningful the check still returns before any hook content is
executed.

Residual, stated plainly: doctor cannot detect a genuinely non-runnable
hook on Windows at all.

Tests cover both arms via the sandboxGOOS override. The Windows arm was
observed red against pre-fix code, reproducing the exact regression text
("seal hook present but not executable — run: chmod +x"), and asserts
which side of the #12 split each case lands in, so it proves the branch
is reachable again rather than only that the wrong FAIL is gone. The two
Unix exec-bit tests now pin the arm explicitly instead of inheriting it
from the test host.
EOF
)"
